title: Direct and Indirect Speech: Greetings and Wishes — Quiz 145
content:
## Direct and Indirect Speech: Greetings and Wishes

Report greetings, good wishes and congratulations.

### Lesson focus

1. The students said, “Good morning, Sir!”
2. My friends said, “Happy Diwali!”
3. She said, “Happy journey!”
4. Father said, “Congratulations, my dear son!”

### Understand the pattern

Greeting and thanking are actions performed through words. Report them with verbs such as greeted, wished and congratulated instead of forcing every example into said that. Name the recipient only when the context identifies that person.

### Worked answers and explanation

The students greeted their teacher. My friends wished the listener a happy Diwali. She wished the traveller a happy journey. Father congratulated his son. In the last example, the original words alone do not say what achievement prompted the congratulations.

### Try another

Report: Ravi said to me, 'Good evening!'

### Suggested answer

Ravi greeted me; or Ravi wished me a good evening. The report names the greeting without inventing a longer conversation.
